projects.title: Bartop arcade (Batocera)
projects.summary: Turn a working laptop into a one-player bartop with a printed or wood cabinet, USB controls, and Batocera on a USB stick or internal drive.
parts: Working laptop (14–17" class fits most docks; confirm your design)
USB arcade joystick + buttons kit (one player)
USB flash drive (16 GB+) for Batocera, or install Batocera to internal storage
3D-printed dock/cabinet OR wood/MDF panels from published plans
Stock laptop AC adapter
Optional: external speakers if the laptop speakers face the wrong way
steps: Decide dock vs gut: dock keeps the laptop intact (easier, reversible); gutting transplants the panel and board into a custom case (harder, better fit).
Download Batocera from batocera.org and write it to USB (or install to disk).
Boot once on a desk, update Batocera, set video mode to the laptop’s native resolution, and test a controller.
Print or cut the cabinet. InventorMike’s Laptop Arcade Dock fits 14–17" laptops; wood plans (WeeCade, Holbrook, Pete Clarke) need measuring your lid thickness and bezel.
Mount the control panel, route USB to the laptop, and secure the chassis so vents stay clear.
Cable-manage the AC adapter; leave a service hatch so you can remove the battery later.
safety: Remove or disconnect the Li-ion battery before drilling, sawing, or soldering near the chassis.
Never puncture, crush, or short a laptop battery — swollen packs go to proper e-waste recycling.
Keep intake/exhaust vents unobstructed; bartops can cook a Core 2 Duo or U-series CPU.
Use the original wattage (or higher, Dell-compatible) AC adapter only.

sections.heading: Installing Batocera
items: Download the x86_64 image from batocera.org/download.
Flash it to a 16 GB+ USB stick or SSD with balenaEtcher or Rufus.
Boot the laptop from USB (F12 on Dell, F12/Enter on Lenovo, F9 on HP, hold Option on Mac). Enable legacy/CSM boot on older BIOSes if it won't show up.
Optional: Main Menu → System Settings → Install Batocera on a new disk to move it to the internal drive (erases that drive).
Copy ROMs you legally own over the network share (\\BATOCERA\share) or to the share partition; add BIOS files as needed.
Map the USB arcade encoder under Controller Settings, and set the video output to the panel's native resolution.

sections.heading: Reusing a bare panel: LVDS/eDP controller boards
items: Read the sticker on the back of the panel (e.g. LP156WH4-TLA1, B156HAB01.0, N140BGE-L23). That part number — not the laptop model — decides which board you need.

Look the part number up on panelook.com (or the maker's datasheet) to confirm interface (LVDS vs eDP), pin count (LVDS often 40-pin; eDP usually 30-pin, 40-pin for touch/high-res), lanes, and backlight type (LED vs CCFL).

Search marketplaces for '<panel part number> controller board' (e.g. 'LP156WH4 driver board'). Generic boards based on the RTD2556/RTD2513 or M.NT68676 chips take HDMI/VGA in and drive LVDS or eDP out; sellers flash firmware for your exact panel, so give them the part number.
Buy the board with its matching panel cable; LVDS cables are not interchangeable with eDP cables. Check pin 1 orientation before powering on.
CCFL-backlit panels (common before ~2009) also need a high-voltage inverter — prefer LED-backlit panels for new builds.
Converter boards that keep the original laptop (e.g. eDP panel into an LVDS ThinkPad) use panel-specific firmware; only listed panels work.

sections.heading: Power options
items: Keep the laptop motherboard: run everything from the original AC adapter (wattage listed on each model page). Simplest; you get the CPU, Wi-Fi, and battery-free operation for free.

Bare panel + controller board: most boards take 12 V DC (typically 2–4 A; check the listing). Use a quality 12 V brick or a 12 V rail in the cabinet; feed a Raspberry Pi or mini PC from a separate 5 V supply or buck converter.
Car/headrest builds: use a fused 12 V accessory feed or a USB-C PD trigger board set to 12 V; never wire straight to the battery without a fuse.
Many laptops run without a battery on AC alone; some (and many Apple models) throttle without one — test before final assembly.
Do not swap in an adapter with a different voltage or connector; matching wattage or higher at the same voltage is fine.

sections.heading: Cooling
items: Keep the original fan and heatsink if you keep the board; clean dust and replace dried thermal paste.
Leave intake and exhaust paths open in the case — at least as much open area as the laptop's own vents; add a 40–80 mm 5 V/12 V fan if the case is closed.
Panel-only builds run cool, but give controller boards and inverters airflow; they get warm.
Monitor temps under load (Batocera: system information; Linux: `sensors`) before closing up.

sections.heading: Battery removal and disposal
items: Power off, unplug AC, then remove or disconnect the battery before any other work. Removable packs slide out; internal packs unplug from the board first.
Glued pouch cells (MacBooks, ultrabooks): use adhesive remover (isopropyl) and plastic tools only — never pry with metal or bend the cell.
A swollen, dented, hot, or hissing pack: stop, move it outdoors onto concrete or into a metal bin with sand, and do not charge it.

Tape the terminals and take packs to a battery drop-off (Call2Recycle locator, Home Depot/Lowe's/Best Buy bins, or municipal hazardous waste). Never put Li-ion in household trash or curbside recycling.
If reusing a healthy pack, keep the original BMS; never charge bare cells without a proper charger.

projects.title: Car headrest monitor
projects.summary: Harvest a laptop LCD (or use a thin 2-in-1) as a rear-seat display with an HDMI/eDP controller board and a headrest mount.
parts: Laptop LCD panel with known interface (LVDS 30/40-pin or eDP)
Matching LCD controller board (HDMI/VGA in) + inverter if CCFL
12 V → board voltage DC-DC (verify board input, often 12 V)
Headrest mount or custom 3D-printed/wood bracket for your seat posts
Automotive fuse tap or accessory power with proper fusing
Optional: USB media player or phone HDMI adapter as the source
steps: Photograph and read the panel sticker (model, resolution, connector) before ordering a controller.
Bench-test panel + controller + power supply on a desk until you get a stable image.
Design a shallow enclosure; keep high-voltage CCFL inverter leads insulated.
Mount to the headrest; strain-relief every cable; fuse the 12 V feed close to the source.
Route cables so airbags, seat travel, and passengers stay clear.
safety: Vehicle electrical work: disconnect the car battery before tapping power; fuse every new circuit.
CCFL inverters produce high voltage — treat as hazardous even when powered down until discharged.
Laptop Li-ion packs do not belong loose in a car cabin; recycle them — power the display from vehicle 12 V via the controller board only.
Never obstruct airbags or headrest safety function; if unsure, use a commercial headrest monitor instead.
